title: Major congenital malformations after first-trimester exposure to ACE inhibitors
authors: Cooper WO, Hernandez-Diaz S, Arbogast PG, Dudley JA, Dyer S, Gideon PS, et al.
population: Infants born 1985 to 2000 enrolled in Tennessee Medicaid without evidence of maternal diabetes: 209 exposed to ACE inhibitors in the first trimester only, 202 to other antihypertensives in the first trimester only and 29,096 unexposed
funder: not read: the publisher page is not accessible. PubMed lists grants HS10384 (Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality) and 223-02-3003 (US Public Health Service).
result: Against infants without antihypertensive exposure, first-trimester ACE inhibitor exposure was associated with major congenital malformations (risk ratio 2.71, 95% CI 1.72 to 4.27), cardiovascular malformations (3.72, 1.89 to 7.30) and central nervous system malformations (4.39, 1.37 to 14.02); first-trimester exposure to other antihypertensives was not (0.66, 0.25 to 1.75). Malformations were confirmed by medical record review.
